findings.issue_text: [BUG] `<%- end if %>` is not valid ERb for terminating the conditional — the trailing `if` either raises a template syntax error or silently opens a new (unintended) conditional whose condition is the following `link_to` line, reordering when the header renders. Every render of the embed/best endpoint either fails to compile the template (ActionView::Template::Error → broken embed iframe on all customer sites) or executes the logo link_to as a conditional expression rather than unconditionally, garbling the header output.

[BUG] `i.content` assumes every feed item has a `content` element, but simple-rss only defines accessors for tags actually present — RSS 2.0 feeds expose `description`, not `content`, so `i.content` raises NoMethodError. With feed_polling_enabled on a standard RSS 2.0 feed (the common case for a 'RSS or ATOM feed' feature), the hourly PollFeed job crashes on the first item and no topics are ever imported; since retry is disabled (sidekiq_options retry: false), the failure is silent until the next hour.

[BUG] Only Gemfile_rails4.lock was regenerated with ruby-readability/simple-rss/guess_html_encoding; the primary Gemfile.lock is not updated in this diff, leaving it inconsistent with the Gemfile. CI/deploys that use the main Gemfile.lock fail Bundler's frozen/locked-gem check ('ruby-readability not in lockfile') or, with `bundle install` allowed to mutate, produce environment drift between the rails3 and rails4 builds.

[ADVISORY] The sprockets directives `//= require ./vendor/normalize` and `//= require ./common/foundation/base` assume those files resolve relative to embed.css.scss's directory, but foundation/base in this codebase typically sits under `common/foundation/*` which itself requires further partials (`_colors`, mixins) that are not safe to compile outside the normal application stylesheet pipeline. Whoever precompiles the embed stylesheet (production asset:precompile) hits a Sprockets file-not-found or missing-variable compile error, breaking the embed page styling in all deployments that precompile assets; a quick manual check of app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/base presence is needed before merge.

[BUG] poll_feed crashes with NoMethodError on nil when a feed item lacks a content element. rss.items.each calls i.content.scrub on an item with no <content> (common in title/summary-only RSS feeds), raising NoMethodError on nil; since sidekiq_options retry: false, the whole hourly poll dies mid-feed and every subsequent item in that feed is silently never imported.

[ADVISORY] Imported content is stored and rendered as raw HTML with skip_validations, bypassing Discourse's sanitization pipeline entirely. Any script/iframe/event-handler markup in the RSS feed (feed_polling_url) or the embeddable host's pages becomes post.cooked verbatim and is served in the embed iframe and the topic page — stored XSS for every reader of the imported topic; the sanitize gem is already a dependency but is never applied to imported content.

[ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values that start with a single leading slash, dropping protocol-relative URLs (//host/path). Feeds that emit protocol-relative links or images produce broken embedded links that resolve against the Discourse host instead of the publisher; the spec only covers the leading-'/' case, so the // case is unverified.

[ADVISORY] feed_key is defined but never used, so the poller re-downloads and re-processes the full feed every hour with no If-Modified-Since / ETag conditional request. Operators of busy feeds pay a full feed fetch plus SHA1 comparison churn per hour; the dead feed_key method signals an intended conditional-fetch requirement that was silently dropped from the implementation.

[ADVISORY] The loading view blindly reloads every 30 seconds with no retry limit and no error state, while the underlying retrieve_topic job can permanently fail. When retrieval never succeeds (feed polling disabled and embed_by_username blank, retrieval throttled for anonymous visitors, or the source page 404s), the embedding site's readers get an infinite reloading iframe that flashes 'Loading Discussion...' every 30 seconds forever — there is no failure criterion anywhere in the design.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage handler accepts any truthy e.data.height (including non-numeric strings and objects) and assigns it directly to iframe.height, and the origin check is a substring match rather than an origin equality check. A malformed message or an origin whose string merely contains discourseUrl's prefix (e.g. discourseUrl 'http://forum' matching origin 'http://forum.evil.com') can resize or manipulate the iframe on publisher pages; no test or acceptance criterion covers the message-validation path at all.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import_remote is the only HTTP-fetch path for the on-demand embed flow yet has zero test coverage — every existing spec (topic_embed_spec) exercises import() with pre-fetched contents, so readability extraction, opts[:title], and open(url) failure modes are unverified. A regression in Readability extraction or a non-HTML/redirecting source URL ships undetected and surfaces only as empty or broken embedded topics on customer sites.

[ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable compares URI(request.referer).host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host with no case normalization or scheme/port handling, and embeddable_host is a free-text setting with no validation. An operator who enters 'EvilTrout.com' or 'http://eviltrout.com' in the setting gets every embed request rejected with InvalidAccess (referer host is lowercase per RFC), producing a 'framed content blocked' 403 that gives no admin-visible hint of misconfiguration; no spec covers these setting-format edge cases.

[ADVISORY] The header branch calls @topic_view.topic.url even in the success-with-zero-posts path where @topic_view.posts is empty but topic is present, yet the whole template assumes @topic_view is always non-nil — but no template path covers TopicView raising when the stored topic_id points to a deleted topic. If the topic behind a TopicEmbed row is deleted (topic_embeds has no dependent destroy / foreign key cascade), topic_id_for_embed returns a stale id, TopicView.new raises RecordNotFound, and the embedding site's iframe renders a 500 forever with no cleanup or fallback to re-retrieval.

[ADVISORY] CGI.unescapeHTML is applied to feed content before it is stored as raw HTML, double-decoding any entity that appears literally in an article's text. Articles containing escaped entities like &amp; or &lt; in their content get unescaped into real markup/characters, corrupting imported posts; no spec covers entity handling in poll_feed.

[BUG] The PR silently deletes the Disqus importer's --category/-c option and posts all imported threads to the default (uncategorized) category. Any operator running `thor disqus:import -p user -c "News"` during the release containing this PR hits Thor aborting on an unknown option (removed method_option), and even after dropping the flag every imported thread lands in uncategorized with no way to select a category — a regression of existing functionality bundled into an unrelated embed-URL PR with no requirement tracing to it.

[BUG] The diff modifies the pre-existing create_top_topics migration to add `force: true`, which drops any existing top_topics table whenever the migration re-runs against a database that already has it. This change is entirely untraceable to the embed-URL intent; on any environment where the table exists (e.g. re-running migrations, redid migrations), `force: true` silently destroys all TopTopic aggregation data. It also indicates the developer is hand-re-running old migrations instead of adding new ones, which itself is a process risk introduced by this PR.

[ADVISORY] The diff touches an unrelated word-count migration with whitespace-only churn (trailing-space removal and a removed trailing newline). Pure out-of-scope noise: the file ends with `\ No newline at end of file`, so this PR both introduces the missing-newline style error it claims to clean up and pollutes git blame for a migration unrelated to embedding. Future archaeologists tracing word-count migrations get a misleading embed-PR commit.

[ADVISORY] The new embedding settings are defined with no admin UI path in this diff: the client locale adds an `embedding` settings tab, but the settings themselves are not exposed anywhere operators can edit them. Staff cannot set embeddable_host, feed_polling_url, or embed_by_username through the admin interface shipped here — only via console — so the entire embed feature is inert until follow-up work that this diff does not include and no requirement covers. Either the locale/tab entry or the settings panel is untraceable scope in this PR.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds embed.js as a standalone asset but adds no route, precompile entry, or documented snippet for sites to actually load it, and no spec covers it. The embeddable-site operator has no shipped way to obtain this script (no `asset_precompile` addition, no /embed.js route, no README instructions), making the client half of the feature untestable from this diff alone — under-scoped relative to the stated embed-handling intent.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import with cook_method raw_html stores the remote page's arbitrary HTML as both raw and cooked with no sanitization anywhere in the pipeline. Post#cook returns raw unmodified (post.rb cook override), and embed/best.html.erb renders `raw post.cooked`, so any script/iframe/onerror attribute in the polled RSS/Atom content or the scraped page executes in the Discourse origin for every visitor of the embed — the embedding site effectively gains script execution on the forum domain.

[BUG] poll_feed calls i.content.scrub and falls back to i.id, but RSS feeds whose items carry only a description (and no content) yield nil for both i.content and i.id, raising NoMethodError on nil.scrub and aborting the entire feed poll. Every hourly PollFeed run dies on the first description-only item with retry: false, so no feed items after that point are ever imported and the embed stays on the 'loading' reload loop forever; any standard RSS 2.0 feed (which uses <description>, not atom:content) hits this immediately.

[BUG] perform_retrieve runs the entire hourly feed poll synchronously inside the per-request RetrieveTopic job by calling Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) instead of enqueuing it. One visitor hitting a new embed URL causes the Sidekiq worker to open the full RSS feed and PostCreator-import every feed item over HTTP with no timeout (open-uri default), so a slow/hung feed URL blocks the worker indefinitely; every uncached embed request repeats the whole-feed fetch, an N-items fan-out for one logical action. It also bypasses sidekiq_options, so retry semantics of the scheduled job are silently lost.

[BUG] On the update path, `post = embed.post` can be nil (post soft-deleted or topic removed) and PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! then raises NoMethodError. A single deleted post referenced by a topic_embed row crashes the RetrieveTopic job / scheduled PollFeed for that feed item every hour (PollFeed has retry: false), so one stale embed blocks nothing but permanently errors and the article never updates.

[ADVISORY] No URL normalization exists between the URL stored by import (i.link from the feed, or readability's fetched URL) and the embed_url looked up by topic_id_for_embed, which is whatever the embedding page passes verbatim. When the feed's <link> differs in form from the page's canonical URL (http vs https, trailing slash, query params like utm_source, FeedBurner redirect links), TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed returns nil forever and the embed shows an endless 'Loading Discussion...' reload loop — the writer path and the comparison path disagree on canonical form.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve uses check-then-insert (SELECT exists, then TopicEmbed.create!) with no rescue on the unique embed_url index, so two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same new URL both pass the exists? check and the loser's create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, failing the job. Two visitors loading the same new article within the same window (the 60s Redis throttle is per-URL but staff bypass it via no_throttle, and the feed path isn't throttled at all) produce a spurious failed job; the data stays consistent only because of the unique index, not the code.

[ADVISORY] feed_key ('feed-modified:<sha1>') is defined and never read or written anywhere, so the feed's modified-since deduplication it implies was never implemented. Every hourly run re-fetches and re-parses the entire feed and re-runs SHA1 comparison per item; the dead method misleads the next editor into believing conditional-fetch caching exists when it does not, and any future 'optimization' assuming the cache key is populated will be a no-op.

[ADVISORY] When topic_id is found, TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) is constructed with no nil/deleted-topic handling and the bare literal 5 for the post count. A topic_embed row whose topic was deleted makes @topic_view nil (or TopicView raises), so /embed/best returns a 500 to every embedding page for that article; and the dimensionless '5' (best-post count) is unreviewable magic — who gets bitten is any operator whose embedded topic is later removed by a moderator.

[ADVISORY] The origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring containment test on two strings that are not canonical forms of each other (e.origin is scheme+host+port with no trailing slash; discourseUrl is whatever the operator pasted, possibly with a path or trailing slash). A discourseUrl configured with any prefix (e.g. 'https://forum.example.com/' works, but an operator setting it to something containing a third-party origin substring silently accepts resize messages from that origin), and the reverse mismatch direction — discourseUrl lacking the exact origin substring — makes the resize handler a silent no-op so the iframe renders at the wrong height; also e.data may be a string from other scripts, and the height is only set once on load with no reflow handling.

[ADVISORY] The header logic tests @topic_view.posts.present? to decide between 'Discussion Highlights' and 'Begin the Discussion', but both branches render a link to @topic_view.topic.url while the else-branch of the controller (loading template) is the only path guarding topic absence — here posts.present? is a proxy for 'topic exists and has replies'. A topic with zero posts (deleted first post) satisfies neither intent cleanly: the 'start discussion' link points at a topic the user cannot actually reply to, and post.user.small_avatar_url / post.user.username in the loop raise on nil user (deleted user) — the view crashes for any feed-imported post whose author account was removed, taking down the embed page for that article.

[ADVISORY] The loading page hardcodes a 30000 ms reload with no cap on retries and no error state. If import never succeeds (invalid feed item, missing embed_by_username user, nil PostRevisor crash), the embedding page reloads the iframe every 30 seconds indefinitely, generating perpetual controller hits that each re-enqueue RetrieveTopic jobs past the 60-second Redis throttle — the dimensionless literal hides that the retry cadence and the throttle window are two independently-tuned constants that can drift.

[ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable relies on the HTTP Referer header for host authorization and sets X-Frame-Options to the non-standard value 'ALLOWALL'. Requests with a spoofed or absent Referer are rejected even from the legitimate embedding host (some browsers strip Referer on downgrade or private mode), and 'ALLOWALL' is not a spec value — browsers that don't recognize it ignore the header entirely while browsers that strictly parse CSP-adjacent frame directives treat the invalid value unpredictably, so the framing posture differs per browser rather than by design.

[ADVISORY] topic_embeds has non-null topic_id and post_id columns with no foreign-key constraints and no uniqueness guard on topic_id, so the schema permits orphan rows and multiple embeds per topic. Deleting a topic or post leaves topic_embed rows whose topic_id_for_embed returns a dead id (leading to the TopicView nil crash), and nothing structurally prevents the same topic being claimed by two embed_urls, which silently splits where replies land when a feed republishes an article under a new link.

[BUG] cook() returns raw unmodified when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing the entire sanitization pipeline for RSS/imported content. TopicEmbed.import stores third-party HTML (Readability-extracted from the embedded site, or arbitrary RSS feed content) as post.cooked with no sanitization; best.html.erb renders it with raw post.cooked, so any <script>/<iframe> in the polled feed or embedded page becomes stored XSS executing on the Discourse origin and on every embedding page.

[BUG] i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element. Any RSS/Atom item lacking <content> (title+link-only feeds are common, e.g. summary-only Atom) crashes the whole poll_feed run after some items imported, and with retry: false the remaining feed items are silently dropped every hour.

[BUG] The update path calls PostRevisor.new(embed.post).revise! without checking embed.post exists, raising NoMethodError when the referenced post was deleted. If a topic's first post is deleted (or the post_id dangles) while the topic_embed row survives, the next poll of that URL crashes with NoMethodError on nil, aborting the rest of the feed poll for all subsequent items.

[BUG] The origin check discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 validates by substring containment, not origin equality. An attacker hosting a page whose origin is a substring of the forum URL (e.g. 'http://forum.example.com.attacker.tld') passes the check and can drive discourse-resize messages; more broadly any origin embedded anywhere in discourseUrl (e.g. in a path) is accepted, letting a malicious embedder control the iframe's rendered height.

[ADVISORY] URL and title are interpolated directly into the post raw string and imported_from footer without escaping. A feed entry whose title or link contains HTML/script text is inserted verbatim into a raw_html post; since cook() returns raw unsanitized, feed-controlled markup is rendered as markup, compounding the raw_html XSS and letting feeds inject arbitrary layout into the forum.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside the embed request's background job, polling the entire RSS feed on every uncached embed hit. Each new embed URL triggers a full feed fetch + N topic imports inside the retrieve_topic job; a crawler hitting many distinct embed/best URLs for a site with feed polling enabled causes an open-uri fetch of the whole feed per URL and hammers the publisher, while the 60s throttle is keyed per embed_url so it never limits feed-level work.

[ADVISORY] An already-shipped migration was edited to add force: true to create_table. Any environment that replays migrations from scratch with an existing top_topics table (or a fresh setup where the schema was loaded and migrations are then re-run) silently drops top_topics and all its rows; modifying a released migration also desyncs environments that already applied it, so schema.rb and migration history diverge.

[ADVISORY] iframe.src is built by string concatenation assuming discourseUrl ends with a slash. Operators who paste the documented snippet with discourseUrl lacking a trailing '/' get a request to e.g. 'https://forum.example.comembed/best?...', a 404 iframe and an apparently broken embed with no diagnostic.

[ADVISORY] post.user is dereferenced unconditionally for small_avatar_url and username. If an embedded post's author was deleted (user_id dangling, common after GDPR-style deletions), the embed view raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 for the entire embed frame on the publisher's page.

[ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites a/img with href/src starting in '/', leaving protocol-relative ('//cdn.example.com/img.png') and relative non-root URLs ('img/wat.jpg') untouched. Imported posts from feeds using relative or protocol-relative asset URLs render broken images/links in the Discourse topic view, degrading the imported content the feature exists to display.

[BUG] The new raw_html cook method returns `raw` completely unsanitized, creating a stored XSS pipeline for imported remote content. RSS feed content (poll_feed.rb line 35: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` — full unfiltered feed item HTML) is imported via TopicEmbed.import with cook_method raw_html and rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 18 (and anywhere cooked posts are displayed). The admin-set feed (or a compromised/malicious embedded site, since import_remote fetches and re-publishes remote readability-extracted HTML) can inject

[BUG] The imported_from footer interpolates `url` into an HTML single-quoted attribute without escaping, allowing attribute-injection XSS. The URL only needs to match `/^https?:\/\//` (start-anchored, not end-anchored), so a feed item link like `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(document.cookie)` passes the regex and breaks out of the href attribute; the crafted attributes execute in the browser of any user viewing the embedded topic or the raw_html-cooked post.

[BUG] absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs/srcs starting with '/', leaving `javascript:` and other scheme-relative URLs intact in the raw HTML that is published unfiltered. A malicious embedded page or feed item containing or passes through import unchanged and is rendered raw in embed/best and the main forum, giving script execution on click — a second XSS vector independent of script tags.

[ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring match, not an origin equality check. Any attacker origin containing the Discourse URL as a substring (e.g. `http://evil.com/?http://forum.example.com` or `http://forum.example.com.evil.com`) passes the check and can drive the embedded iframe's height; the current payload only sets height so impact is cosmetic spoofing, but the check is structurally wrong for any future message types.

[ADVISORY] TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve invokes the entire PollFeed job synchronously on every un-throttled retrieve, allowing a request-driven amplification of server-side fetches of the admin-configured feed_polling_url. Any visitor to the embedding site (no authentication required by the embed endpoint beyond the referer host, which anyone can forge by hosting a page under a URL whose referer is the embeddable host) triggers a full feed re-fetch per minute per URL; combined with the 1-minute HTTP cache expiry on embed/best, this lets an attacker make the Discourse server issue repeated outbound fetches, and the content fetched is republished raw (see the XSS findings), so a feed/host compromise directly executes script on the forum.

[ADVISORY] The embed endpoint's only authz gate is the Referer header, which is client-controlled and absent/trivially spoofable in non-browser HTTP clients. An attacker using curl (no Referer? that's rejected — but a forged Referer of the embeddable_host is trivial) reads the imported topic content through /embed/best and enqueues retrieve jobs; since the endpoint also skips XHR/preload filters and serves full post bodies to anonymous traffic, it doubles as a scraping/DoS vector against the forum's topic view rendering with only a 1-minute cache.

[ADVISORY] The only success-path test stubs out poll_feed itself (poller.expects(:poll_feed).once), so the entire body of Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed — SimpleRSS parsing, the item link/id fallback (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`), CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and TopicEmbed.import delegation — has zero test coverage in this diff. A regression in poll_feed's URL fallback or feed parsing ships green; feed-imported topics silently stop being created or import with wrong URLs, and the poller's inline invocation from TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve (which passes no args and relies on SiteSetting stubs that the real job won't have stubbed) is never exercised against real behavior.

[ADVISORY] Both throttle tests stub retrieved_recently? (returns(false)/returns(true)), so the actual Redis setnx/expire throttle logic in topic_retriever.rb lines 25-33 is never executed by any test in the diff. If the setnx/expire pair is broken (e.g. key never expired, or expire dropped so the throttle becomes permanent), every spec passes; production embeds then retrieve at most once per embed_url ever, or hammer the source site on every request, and the no_throttle staff bypass path is likewise unverified.

[ADVISORY] The 'success' context tests assert only that mocks were constructed and called (TopicRetriever/TopicView fully mocked with expects) and hide the real assertions in an `after` block, so no test verifies the rendered output of best.html.erb/loading.html.erb or that render 'loading' is actually reached. A regression in the views (e.g. the `<%- end if %>` conditional in best.html.erb rendering the wrong branch, or the loading view failing to render when topic_id is nil) passes the entire controller spec; a broken example body can also be masked because the after-hook assertion runs after the example's own failure, producing confusing double-failure or masking the real one.

[ADVISORY] The 'Supports updating the post' test asserts only cooked content via a regex and never asserts that TopicEmbed#content_sha1 was updated, nor is the unchanged-content path (revisor must NOT run) tested at all. Deleting `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` in TopicEmbed.import passes the suite; every subsequent poll then re-revises the post on every feed cycle, spamming revisions and edit notifications, with no test failure.

[ADVISORY] The test named 'is 404 without an embed_url' asserts only `response.should_not be_success`, which passes for any error status (params.require raises ParameterMissing, rendered as 400, not 404). The test name documents a status contract the assertion never checks; a change that turns this into a 500 keeps the suite green while the documented 404/4xx contract is silently broken.

[BUG] absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs: href/src values starting with '//' (e.g. '//cdn.example.com/img.jpg') match `starts_with?('/')` and get rewritten to 'http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.jpg', and the only test (topic_embed_spec.rb:35) uses start_with? on a fixture containing solely root-relative paths, so this branch is never exercised. Any RSS/embedded article using protocol-relative asset or link URLs (common in feeds) imports with broken links and broken images on the embedded topic, and the test suite gives false confidence because its assertion data table only covers cases the code already handles.

[BUG] `force: true` was added to the already-shipped CreateTopTopics migration, making a previously idempotent migration destructive on re-run. Any environment that re-runs this migration (db:rollback followed by re-migrate, db:migrate:redo, or a re-created schema_migrations entry) silently executes DROP TABLE top_topics and destroys all computed top-topic ranking data with no backup/export step.

[BUG] A shipped migration file was edited (whitespace/no-trailing-newline changes), altering its checksum. Environments that fingerprint migration contents (or schema dump tools comparing migration file hashes) flag the migration as tampered; more importantly it establishes the pattern of editing shipped migrations in this PR, which is how the CreateTopTopics force: true data-loss hazard was introduced.

[ADVISORY] `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` uses force on a table creation, so a re-run of the migration drops and recreates the table rather than failing loudly. If this migration is ever re-applied on a populated database (rollback/re-migrate, restored schema_migrations), all TopicEmbed rows — the mapping between embed URLs and imported topics — are destroyed, orphaning the imported topics and making feed polling re-import duplicates.

[ADVISORY] The update path fetches `embed.post` with no nil check, and the create path returns `post` even when `creator.create` failed (post creation errors are swallowed because `if post.present?` guards only the TopicEmbed insert, not the return). When the referenced post was deleted (e.g. via a forum purge) while the topic_embed row remains, the next feed poll crashes PostRevisor.new(nil) with NoMethodError, so the hourly PollFeed job (retry: false) dies on that item and all subsequent feed items never import.

[ADVISORY] The Disqus import path was rewritten to TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping the explicit `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` and the category option, so imported topics lose their original timestamps and category assignment. Anyone re-running the Disqus import after this change gets topics dated at import time and uncategorized — a field-fidelity loss relative to the previous behavior; a rollback to the old code cannot recover the original created_at values once imported.

[ADVISORY] `poll_feed` calls `i.content.scrub` and `i.title` without nil guards, and passes a possibly-nil title to PostCreator. A single RSS item lacking a content or title element raises NoMethodError inside the hourly PollFeed job (retry: false), aborting the loop so all remaining items in the feed — including valid ones ordered after it — are never imported until the next hourly run hits the same item again.

[BUG] `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is invoked with no timeout and no size cap, so a hung or slow feed server blocks the worker indefinitely. A feed host that accepts the TCP connection but never responds hangs the PollFeed job (and any RetrieveTopic job that runs it synchronously, see topic_retriever.rb:40) for as long as the OS default socket timeout allows, stalling sidekiq workers; because `sidekiq_options retry: false` there is also no retry, so the poll silently never completes.

[BUG] `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element (Atom entries with only `<summary>`, plain RSS 2.0 items with only `<description>`), and the whole `rss.items.each` loop aborts on the first such item. One malformed/short item anywhere in the feed stops processing of every subsequent item in that poll — all later articles are silently dropped while the job 'succeeds'; with `retry: false` the work is lost until the next hour and then fails the same way, so the tail of the feed is never imported.

[BUG] `TopicEmbed.import` returns nil with no log and no error result when the URL doesn't match `/^https?:///`, so callers like the disqus importer and PollFeed silently skip the item while treating the run as success. The disqus import path (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor` now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote` → `import`) silently skips any thread whose link is not http(s) — the importer prints 'Creating ...' then skips it, and PollFeed drops every non-http item with no error surfaced; operators see a completed import with missing content and nothing to debug.

[BUG] `fetch_http` crashes with NoMethodError on nil when `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is blank, because `.downcase` is called before the blank check that PollFeed's `execute` performs but this path does not. With embeddable_host set but embed_by_username blank (a configuration that the /embed/best endpoint's `ensure_embeddable` filter does not reject), the RetrieveTopic job dies with an unhandled exception; the user's browser sits on the loading page and reloads every 30s forever with no error ever surfaced.

[BUG] The 60-second throttle key is committed via `setnx` before the retrieval is attempted, so a failed fetch burns the throttle and subsequent requests no-op 'successfully' for 60 seconds. When `fetch_http`/`import_remote` raises (network error, readability failure) or silently returns nil (user blank, invalid URL), the redis key is already set, so every retry from the embedding page's 30s reload hits `retrieved_recently?` true and does nothing — the user is stuck on the 'Loading Discussion' page reloading indefinitely with the failure completely invisible.

[ADVISORY] `perform_retrieve` runs the entire PollFeed synchronously inside the RetrieveTopic job (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), so one embed page view triggers a full feed download and a TopicEmbed.import for every feed item. Each first-time embed view pays the cost of importing the whole RSS feed (N remote-fetched articles if the feed doesn't contain the URL and it falls through to fetch_http — a full second remote fetch per item); a site with a large feed gets a long-running job per new embed URL, multiplying outbound requests and blocking workers; if PollFeed raises, fetch_http never runs for that URL.

[ADVISORY] The origin check uses substring containment (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`), and the resize handler is the only feedback channel for iframe height.
