adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, each item does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is nil (e.g., RSS items that only have `<description>`), this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil.scrub`, aborting the poll. The code also falls back to `i.id` for the URL when `i.link` is blank/invalid, but does not guard against `i.id` being nil, which could further prevent importing. With `sidekiq_options retry: false`, this failure would stop subsequent items from being processed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] perform_retrieve runs the entire hourly feed poll synchronously inside the per-request RetrieveTopic job by calling Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) instead of enqueuing it. One visitor hitting a new embed URL causes the Sidekiq worker to open the full RSS feed and PostCreator-import every feed item over HTTP with no timeout (open-uri default), so a slow/hung feed URL blocks the worker indefinitely; every uncached embed request repeats the whole-feed fetch, an N-items fan-out for one logical action. It also bypasses sidekiq_options, so retry semantics of the scheduled job are silently lost.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true (lib/topic_retriever.rb), instead of enqueuing/scheduling it. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) which uses open-uri with no explicit timeouts and then iterates `rss.items.each` importing each item. Since RetrieveTopic runs in Sidekiq (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) and is enqueued from embed requests (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), a single new embed request can block a Sidekiq worker on a slow/hung feed fetch and fan-out through all items. Also, calling `new.execute` bypasses the scheduled job’s Sidekiq configuration (`sidekiq_options retry: false`) and scheduling semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On the update path, `post = embed.post` can be nil (post soft-deleted or topic removed) and PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! then raises NoMethodError. A single deleted post referenced by a topic_embed row crashes the RetrieveTopic job / scheduled PollFeed for that feed item every hour (PollFeed has retry: false), so one stale embed blocks nothing but permanently errors and the article never updates.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update branch does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` when `content_sha1` changes. Since `topic_embeds.post_id` has no foreign key constraint in the migration (only `null: false`), it is possible for the referenced Post row to be missing (e.g., hard-deleted), making `embed.post` return `nil`. That would lead to `PostRevisor.new(nil)` and likely a runtime error during `revise!`, which would crash `Jobs::PollFeed` / `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` when attempting to update that embed URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No URL normalization exists between the URL stored by import (i.link from the feed, or readability's fetched URL) and the embed_url looked up by topic_id_for_embed, which is whatever the embedding page passes verbatim. When the feed's <link> differs in form from the page's canonical URL (http vs https, trailing slash, query params like utm_source, FeedBurner redirect links), TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed returns nil forever and the embed shows an endless 'Loading Discussion...' reload loop — the writer path and the comparison path disagree on canonical form.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does store and look up `embed_url` via exact string match with no normalization: `TopicEmbed.import` persists `embed_url: url` verbatim, while `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` does `where(embed_url: embed_url)` and the controller uses `params.require(:embed_url)` directly. So differing URL forms (http/https, trailing slash, tracking params, redirector links) can prevent matching an already-imported embed and lead to extra/duplicate topics or unnecessary re-import attempts. However, the finding’s claim that this results in `topic_id_for_embed` returning nil “forever” and an endless loading loop is not strictly verifiable from the diff because `RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever` will attempt `import_remote` for the passed URL and can create a new `TopicEmbed` for that exact URL, resolving the load (unless fetch fails for other reasons).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] perform_retrieve uses check-then-insert (SELECT exists, then TopicEmbed.create!) with no rescue on the unique embed_url index, so two concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs for the same new URL both pass the exists? check and the loser's create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, failing the job. Two visitors loading the same new article within the same window (the 60s Redis throttle is per-URL but staff bypass it via no_throttle, and the feed path isn't throttled at all) produce a spurious failed job; the data stays consistent only because of the unique index, not the code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a classic race: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve does `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and then later calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import`. In TopicEmbed.import it again does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank executes `TopicEmbed.create!` under a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (added in `create_topic_embeds`). With two concurrent jobs/requests for the same new URL, both can observe no row and both attempt `create!`; the loser will raise an exception (e.g., RecordNotUnique) with no rescue shown, failing the job even though the unique index keeps data consistent. This is directly verifiable from the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key ('feed-modified:<sha1>') is defined and never read or written anywhere, so the feed's modified-since deduplication it implies was never implemented. Every hourly run re-fetches and re-parses the entire feed and re-runs SHA1 comparison per item; the dead method misleads the next editor into believing conditional-fetch caching exists when it does not, and any future 'optimization' assuming the cache key is populated will be a no-op.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (computes a Redis key based on `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) but is never referenced by `execute` or `poll_feed`, and there are no Redis reads/writes using it in this diff. The job always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` on each run, so there is no conditional-fetch/dedup behavior despite the presence of `feed_key`, making it misleading dead code rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When topic_id is found, TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) is constructed with no nil/deleted-topic handling and the bare literal 5 for the post count. A topic_embed row whose topic was deleted makes @topic_view nil (or TopicView raises), so /embed/best returns a 500 to every embedding page for that article; and the dimensionless '5' (best-post count) is unreviewable magic — who gets bitten is any operator whose embedded topic is later removed by a moderator.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns a topic_id, the code unconditionally does `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` with no check that the topic actually exists (or wasn’t deleted) and no rescue/fallback. Since topic_id_for_embed just plucks an integer from topic_embeds (no FK enforcement shown) a stale topic_id can occur; in that case TopicView.new is likely to raise (e.g., record not found), causing a 500 for /embed/best. The “magic 5” is a maintainability concern, but the missing deleted-topic handling is a real failure mode grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring containment test on two strings that are not canonical forms of each other (e.origin is scheme+host+port with no trailing slash; discourseUrl is whatever the operator pasted, possibly with a path or trailing slash). A discourseUrl configured with any prefix (e.g. 'https://forum.example.com/' works, but an operator setting it to something containing a third-party origin substring silently accepts resize messages from that origin), and the reverse mismatch direction — discourseUrl lacking the exact origin substring — makes the resize handler a silent no-op so the iframe renders at the wrong height; also e.data may be a string from other scripts, and the height is only set once on load with no reflow handling.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message origin validation is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is a non-canonical substring test rather than an exact origin comparison. Since `e.origin` is strictly `scheme://host[:port]` while `discourseUrl` is an operator-provided arbitrary string (may include trailing slash/path/port), this can (a) incorrectly reject legitimate messages (e.g., port/format mismatch) causing the iframe height never to update, and (b) incorrectly accept messages from an unintended origin if that origin string appears as a substring within the configured `discourseUrl`. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The header logic tests @topic_view.posts.present? to decide between 'Discussion Highlights' and 'Begin the Discussion', but both branches render a link to @topic_view.topic.url while the else-branch of the controller (loading template) is the only path guarding topic absence — here posts.present? is a proxy for 'topic exists and has replies'. A topic with zero posts (deleted first post) satisfies neither intent cleanly: the 'start discussion' link points at a topic the user cannot actually reply to, and post.user.small_avatar_url / post.user.username in the loop raise on nil user (deleted user) — the view crashes for any feed-imported post whose author account was removed, taking down the embed page for that article.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the embed view calling `post.user.small_avatar_url`/`post.user.username` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb) without a nil guard, but the finding’s core claim—that this will crash “for any feed-imported post whose author account was removed”—is not supported by the diff: feed import creates posts as the single configured `embed_by_username` user (Jobs::PollFeed -> TopicEmbed.import(user, ...) and TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, ...)), not per-feed authors. Also, the “topic with zero posts (deleted first post)” scenario and inability to reply are speculative and not verifiable from this PR alone; the controller always builds `@topic_view` only when a `topic_id` exists, and `posts.present?` is only used to change copy, not to guard topic existence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading page hardcodes a 30000 ms reload with no cap on retries and no error state. If import never succeeds (invalid feed item, missing embed_by_username user, nil PostRevisor crash), the embedding page reloads the iframe every 30 seconds indefinitely, generating perpetual controller hits that each re-enqueue RetrieveTopic jobs past the 60-second Redis throttle — the dimensionless literal hides that the retry cadence and the throttle window are two independently-tuned constants that can drift.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loading view that unconditionally reloads every 30s (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` uses `setTimeout(..., 30000); document.location.reload();`) with no retry cap or failure UI. In `EmbedController#best`, whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns nil it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: ...)` and renders `loading`, so repeated reloads can keep hitting the controller and re-enqueueing jobs until an embed exists. The PR does have a 60s Redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, but that throttle prevents `perform_retrieve` inside the job, not the enqueue itself; the finding’s “past the 60-second throttle” wording is overstated, but the underlying concern (unbounded reload loop causing repeated requests/job enqueues) is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable relies on the HTTP Referer header for host authorization and sets X-Frame-Options to the non-standard value 'ALLOWALL'. Requests with a spoofed or absent Referer are rejected even from the legitimate embedding host (some browsers strip Referer on downgrade or private mode), and 'ALLOWALL' is not a spec value — browsers that don't recognize it ignore the header entirely while browsers that strictly parse CSP-adjacent frame directives treat the invalid value unpredictably, so the framing posture differs per browser rather than by design.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, authorization is based solely on `request.referer` host comparison (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), which will reject legitimate embeds when the Referer header is absent/stripped, and is not a trustworthy security signal because clients can spoof it. Additionally, it sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`, which is not a standard X-Frame-Options directive (standard values are DENY/SAMEORIGIN/ALLOW-FROM), so browsers may ignore or handle it inconsistently. Both behaviors are directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] topic_embeds has non-null topic_id and post_id columns with no foreign-key constraints and no uniqueness guard on topic_id, so the schema permits orphan rows and multiple embeds per topic. Deleting a topic or post leaves topic_embed rows whose topic_id_for_embed returns a dead id (leading to the TopicView nil crash), and nothing structurally prevents the same topic being claimed by two embed_urls, which silently splits where replies land when a feed republishes an article under a new link.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` creates `topic_embeds` with non-null `topic_id`/`post_id` but only adds a unique index on `embed_url` (no FK constraints, no uniqueness/index on `topic_id`/`post_id`), and the model `TopicEmbed` has plain `belongs_to` associations with no `dependent` cleanup. From the diff alone, this does mean the schema permits orphaned `topic_embeds` rows and multiple rows pointing at the same topic/post. However, the finding’s downstream claim about a guaranteed “TopicView nil crash” after deletions isn’t verifiable from this diff (TopicView behavior and whether topics/posts are hard-deleted aren’t shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] cook() returns raw unmodified when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing the entire sanitization pipeline for RSS/imported content. TopicEmbed.import stores third-party HTML (Readability-extracted from the embedded site, or arbitrary RSS feed content) as post.cooked with no sanitization; best.html.erb renders it with raw post.cooked, so any <script>/<iframe> in the polled feed or embedded page becomes stored XSS executing on the Discourse origin and on every embedding page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `:raw_html` cook method that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` immediately (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing the normal cooking/filtering pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook` + plugin filters). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts from third-party `contents` (RSS via `SimpleRSS.parse ... i.content.scrub` in `Jobs::PollFeed`, and remote HTML via `Readability::Document` in `import_remote`) and sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so that HTML is stored/served without sanitization. The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (and since `cooked == raw` for `raw_html`), so malicious tags/attributes from RSS content can become stored XSS on the Discourse origin and in embeds. Readability limits tags/attrs, but RSS path has no such restriction in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element. Any RSS/Atom item lacking <content> (title+link-only feeds are common, e.g. summary-only Atom) crashes the whole poll_feed run after some items imported, and with retry: false the remaining feed items are silently dropped every hour.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (e.g., title/link-only items), `i.content` can be `nil`, and calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the loop and thus the whole job run. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a crash would not be retried, matching the finding’s claim that remaining items are skipped until the next schedule.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The update path calls PostRevisor.new(embed.post).revise! without checking embed.post exists, raising NoMethodError when the referenced post was deleted. If a topic's first post is deleted (or the post_id dangles) while the topic_embed row survives, the next poll of that URL crashes with NoMethodError on nil, aborting the rest of the feed poll for all subsequent items.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update branch assumes `embed.post` exists: `post = embed.post` then (if content changed) `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)` with no nil-guard. If the `topic_embeds` row remains but its `post_id` points to a deleted/missing post, `embed.post` will be `nil`, and passing that into `PostRevisor`/calling methods on it is very likely to raise at runtime. `Jobs::PollFeed` does not rescue per-item failures, so an exception would abort the rest of the feed processing loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The origin check discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 validates by substring containment, not origin equality. An attacker hosting a page whose origin is a substring of the forum URL (e.g. 'http://forum.example.com.attacker.tld') passes the check and can drive discourse-resize messages; more broadly any origin embedded anywhere in discourseUrl (e.g. in a path) is accepted, letting a malicious embedder control the iframe's rendered height.

adjudication.rationale: In new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is a substring containment check, not an origin equality check, so any `e.origin` that happens to appear anywhere inside `discourseUrl` will be accepted. A correct check would compare against the parsed origin of `discourseUrl` (scheme+host+port) rather than using `indexOf`, otherwise unrelated origins can pass in some constructed cases and drive `discourse-resize` behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] URL and title are interpolated directly into the post raw string and imported_from footer without escaping. A feed entry whose title or link contains HTML/script text is inserted verbatim into a raw_html post; since cook() returns raw unsanitized, feed-controlled markup is rendered as markup, compounding the raw_html XSS and letting feeds inject arbitrary layout into the forum.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method that bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and embedded view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Feed/remote content is imported into such posts: `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and uses `contents` from RSS (`SimpleRSS.parse` + `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) or from `ruby-readability` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` appends an HTML footer that interpolates `url` directly into an `<a href='#{url}'>` without escaping. Since `url` is only checked with `/^https?\:\/\//`, it can still contain quotes/HTML-breaking characters, and the feed-controlled `contents` can include arbitrary markup. Combined, this enables XSS/markup injection in `raw_html` posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] perform_retrieve runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside the embed request's background job, polling the entire RSS feed on every uncached embed hit. Each new embed URL triggers a full feed fetch + N topic imports inside the retrieve_topic job; a crawler hitting many distinct embed/best URLs for a site with feed polling enabled causes an open-uri fetch of the whole feed per URL and hammers the publisher, while the 60s throttle is keyed per embed_url so it never limits feed-level work.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve synchronously calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to `fetch_http`. This is invoked from the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` background job for each uncached `embed_url` (EmbedController enqueues retrieve_topic when no embed exists). The throttle in `retrieved_recently?` is keyed by `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so many distinct embed URLs can each trigger a full feed fetch/parse/import cycle (`Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and iterates items) rather than throttling feed-level work. This is a concrete performance/architecture issue grounded in the diff, though not a direct correctness failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] An already-shipped migration was edited to add force: true to create_table. Any environment that replays migrations from scratch with an existing top_topics table (or a fresh setup where the schema was loaded and migrations are then re-run) silently drops top_topics and all its rows; modifying a released migration also desyncs environments that already applied it, so schema.rb and migration history diverge.

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can cause silent data loss when migrations are replayed in an environment where `top_topics` already exists. Editing an existing (previously present) migration also risks divergence between environments that already ran it and those that haven’t.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] iframe.src is built by string concatenation assuming discourseUrl ends with a slash. Operators who paste the documented snippet with discourseUrl lacking a trailing '/' get a request to e.g. 'https://forum.example.comembed/best?...', a 404 iframe and an apparently broken embed with no diagnostic.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `iframe.src` is constructed via `discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ...`. Nothing in the diff normalizes `discourseUrl` (e.g., ensuring it ends with `/`). If `discourseUrl` is configured as `https://forum.example.com` (no trailing slash), the resulting URL becomes `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which would be an invalid path and likely 404, breaking embeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] post.user is dereferenced unconditionally for small_avatar_url and username. If an embedded post's author was deleted (user_id dangling, common after GDPR-style deletions), the embed view raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 for the entire embed frame on the publisher's page.

adjudication.rationale: In the new embed view `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the template unconditionally dereferences `post.user` (`post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username`). If `post.user` can ever be `nil` (e.g., deleted/invalid user association), this will raise `NoMethodError` and break the entire embed frame rendering with a 500. The diff does not add any guard/fallback for missing users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] absolutize_urls only rewrites a/img with href/src starting in '/', leaving protocol-relative ('//cdn.example.com/img.png') and relative non-root URLs ('img/wat.jpg') untouched. Imported posts from feeds using relative or protocol-relative asset URLs render broken images/links in the Discourse topic view, degrading the imported content the feature exists to display.

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` claims to “Convert any relative URLs to absolute”, but it only rewrites `` / `` values that `start_with?('/')`. Protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn...`) and relative non-root URLs (`img/wat.jpg`, `../img.png`) are left unchanged (see `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` and same for `src`), so imported HTML containing those forms will still be relative in the rendered Discourse post and can resolve incorrectly (typically against the Discourse host), breaking links/assets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new raw_html cook method returns `raw` completely unsanitized, creating a stored XSS pipeline for imported remote content. RSS feed content (poll_feed.rb line 35: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` — full unfiltered feed item HTML) is imported via TopicEmbed.import with cook_method raw_html and rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 18 (and anywhere cooked posts are displayed). The admin-set feed (or a compromised/malicious embedded site, since import_remote fetches and re-publishes remote readability-extracted HTML) can inject

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` directly (`app/models/post.rb`), bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` from RSS/remote HTML (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). The RSS path explicitly imports `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` without any sanitization/whitelisting (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`). This creates a stored XSS vector for imported content. Even the readability path only constrains tags/attributes, and `href`/`src` values (e.g., `javascript:`) are not shown to be filtered in this diff, so unsanitized scriptable HTML can persist and be rendered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The imported_from footer interpolates `url` into an HTML single-quoted attribute without escaping, allowing attribute-injection XSS. The URL only needs to match `/^https?:\/\//` (start-anchored, not end-anchored), so a feed item link like `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(document.cookie)` passes the regex and breaks out of the href attribute; the crafted attributes execute in the browser of any user viewing the embedded topic or the raw_html-cooked post.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends `"#{url}"` into `contents` (HTML) without escaping (`topic_embed.rb`, `import`). The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows URLs containing a single quote and additional attributes (e.g., `http://x/' onmouseover='...`) because the regex is only start-anchored. Since imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `:raw_html`, the HTML is rendered unsanitized (`post.rb`), making this a straightforward attribute-injection XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs/srcs starting with '/', leaving `javascript:` and other scheme-relative URLs intact in the raw HTML that is published unfiltered. A malicious embedded page or feed item containing or passes through import unchanged and is rendered raw in embed/best and the main forum, giving script execution on click — a second XSS vector independent of script tags.

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicEmbed.import`, imported `contents` are stored as `raw` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (see `PostCreator.new(..., raw: ..., cook_method: ...)`). `Post#cook` then returns `raw` directly for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`.

`TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` only rewrites `href`/`src` values that `start_with?('/')` and leaves all other schemes intact, including potentially dangerous `javascript:` or `data:` URLs. Therefore a feed/article containing `<a href='javascript:...'>` or similar will be imported unchanged and rendered as raw HTML, creating an XSS vector (at least on click for `javascript:`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postMessage origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring match, not an origin equality check. Any attacker origin containing the Discourse URL as a substring (e.g. `http://evil.com/?http://forum.example.com` or `http://forum.example.com.evil.com`) passes the check and can drive the embedded iframe's height; the current payload only sets height so impact is cosmetic spoofing, but the check is structurally wrong for any future message types.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same flaw: using `indexOf` for origin validation is a substring check that can be bypassed by malicious origins like `forum.example.com.evil.com` or similar, matching the golden concern about `evil-discourseUrl.com` passing the check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve invokes the entire PollFeed job synchronously on every un-throttled retrieve, allowing a request-driven amplification of server-side fetches of the admin-configured feed_polling_url. Any visitor to the embedding site (no authentication required by the embed endpoint beyond the referer host, which anyone can forge by hosting a page under a URL whose referer is the embeddable host) triggers a full feed re-fetch per minute per URL; combined with the 1-minute HTTP cache expiry on embed/best, this lets an attacker make the Discourse server issue repeated outbound fetches, and the content fetched is republished raw (see the XSS findings), so a feed/host compromise directly executes script on the forum.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a request-accessible path that can trigger server-side outbound fetch amplification. `EmbedController#best` is unauthenticated aside from a Referer host check (`ensure_embeddable`) and enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` whenever no embed exists. That job calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which (when not throttled by `retrieved_recently?`) calls `perform_retrieve`, and `perform_retrieve` synchronously invokes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, causing an outbound fetch of the configured feed. Because throttling is keyed by `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), an attacker can vary `embed_url` values under the allowed host to force repeated feed fetches and processing, effectively turning `/embed/best` traffic into repeated outbound requests/CPU work. This is a security/DoS-style defect introduced by the new embedding/feed retrieval flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embed endpoint's only authz gate is the Referer header, which is client-controlled and absent/trivially spoofable in non-browser HTTP clients. An attacker using curl (no Referer? that's rejected — but a forged Referer of the embeddable_host is trivial) reads the imported topic content through /embed/best and enqueues retrieve jobs; since the endpoint also skips XHR/preload filters and serves full post bodies to anonymous traffic, it doubles as a scraping/DoS vector against the forum's topic view rendering with only a 1-minute cache.

adjudication.rationale: The new /embed/best endpoint’s access control is `ensure_embeddable`, which only checks `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). Since `Referer` is client-supplied and trivially forgeable, a non-browser client can bypass the intended host restriction by sending a spoofed Referer and then (a) render topic content via `TopicView.new(..., current_user, {best: 5})` and `raw post.cooked` in the view, and/or (b) trigger background work because when no embed exists it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)`. The diff also explicitly skips `:check_xhr`/`:preload_json`, making it a lightweight, unauthenticated surface. While `TopicRetriever` throttles per-URL, the referer-based gate itself is the only shown authorization check and is not trustworthy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only success-path test stubs out poll_feed itself (poller.expects(:poll_feed).once), so the entire body of Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed — SimpleRSS parsing, the item link/id fallback (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`), CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and TopicEmbed.import delegation — has zero test coverage in this diff. A regression in poll_feed's URL fallback or feed parsing ships green; feed-imported topics silently stop being created or import with wrong URLs, and the poller's inline invocation from TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve (which passes no args and relies on SiteSetting stubs that the real job won't have stubbed) is never exercised against real behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, Jobs::PollFeed introduces nontrivial logic in #poll_feed (SimpleRSS.parse open(...), per-item URL fallback to i.id when i.link is blank/non-http(s), CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), and TopicEmbed.import delegation). The added spec (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb) only asserts that #execute calls #poll_feed via `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once` and does not exercise any of #poll_feed’s internal behavior, so regressions in parsing/fallback/import could ship with green tests. The related invocation from TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) is also not covered by any test path that runs the real poll_feed behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Both throttle tests stub retrieved_recently? (returns(false)/returns(true)), so the actual Redis setnx/expire throttle logic in topic_retriever.rb lines 25-33 is never executed by any test in the diff. If the setnx/expire pair is broken (e.g. key never expired, or expire dropped so the throttle becomes permanent), every spec passes; production embeds then retrieve at most once per embed_url ever, or hammer the source site on every request, and the no_throttle staff bypass path is likewise unverified.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the two “valid host” examples stub `retrieved_recently?` to return `false`/`true`, so the real throttle implementation in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (the `$redis.setnx` + `$redis.expire` behavior and the `@opts[:no_throttle]` bypass) is never executed by any test in the diff. This is a concrete coverage gap for newly added, behavior-critical logic; a regression in the Redis throttle semantics would not be caught.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'success' context tests assert only that mocks were constructed and called (TopicRetriever/TopicView fully mocked with expects) and hide the real assertions in an `after` block, so no test verifies the rendered output of best.html.erb/loading.html.erb or that render 'loading' is actually reached. A regression in the views (e.g. the `<%- end if %>` conditional in best.html.erb rendering the wrong branch, or the loading view failing to render when topic_id is nil) passes the entire controller spec; a broken example body can also be masked because the after-hook assertion runs after the example's own failure, producing confusing double-failure or masking the real one.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the "success" context examples primarily assert mocked interactions (e.g., expects on TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed and TopicView.new / TopicRetriever.new) and the only concrete controller-response assertions (response success + X-Frame-Options == "ALLOWALL") are placed in an `after` hook. There is no assertion about which template is rendered (`best` vs `loading`) or any rendered content from app/views/embed/best.html.erb or loading.html.erb, so regressions in those views/branches could go undetected. Also, using an `after` hook for core assertions can lead to confusing double-failures because it runs even when an example fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'Supports updating the post' test asserts only cooked content via a regex and never asserts that TopicEmbed#content_sha1 was updated, nor is the unchanged-content path (revisor must NOT run) tested at all. Deleting `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` in TopicEmbed.import passes the suite; every subsequent poll then re-revises the post on every feed cycle, spamming revisions and edit notifications, with no test failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the changed-content path updates `embed.content_sha1` via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` after revising the post. The spec `"Supports updating the post"` in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` only asserts `post.cooked` matches `/new contents/` and never checks that the associated `TopicEmbed` row’s `content_sha1` was updated. There is also no spec covering the unchanged-content path (where `content_sha1 == embed.content_sha1` and `PostRevisor` should not run). This is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap for nontrivial update logic, not a demonstrated runtime defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test named 'is 404 without an embed_url' asserts only `response.should_not be_success`, which passes for any error status (params.require raises ParameterMissing, rendered as 400, not 404). The test name documents a status contract the assertion never checks; a change that turns this into a 500 keeps the suite green while the documented 404/4xx contract is silently broken.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the example named `"is 404 without an embed_url"` only asserts `response.should_not be_success` after `get :best` with no params. In `EmbedController#best`, `params.require(:embed_url)` will raise when missing, but the spec never asserts the promised status code/contract (404 vs 400 vs 500), so the test name can be misleading and the suite could remain green even if the specific error behavior changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs: href/src values starting with '//' (e.g. '//cdn.example.com/img.jpg') match `starts_with?('/')` and get rewritten to 'http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.jpg', and the only test (topic_embed_spec.rb:35) uses start_with? on a fixture containing solely root-relative paths, so this branch is never exercised. Any RSS/embedded article using protocol-relative asset or link URLs (common in feeds) imports with broken links and broken images on the embedded topic, and the test suite gives false confidence because its assertion data table only covers cases the code already handles.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both `href` and `src` are rewritten whenever they `start_with?('/')`, and the rewrite uses `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` / `src.sub(/^\/+/, '')`. This will treat protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.jpg` as relative and rewrite them to `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/img.jpg`, which is incorrect and will break imported links/assets. The existing spec only covers single-slash root-relative paths (`/hello`, `/images/wat.jpg`) and does not cover the `//...` protocol-relative case, so the bug would not be caught by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `force: true` was added to the already-shipped CreateTopTopics migration, making a previously idempotent migration destructive on re-run. Any environment that re-runs this migration (db:rollback followed by re-migrate, db:migrate:redo, or a re-created schema_migrations entry) silently executes DROP TABLE top_topics and destroys all computed top-topic ranking data with no backup/export step.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before creating it, which makes re-running that migration destructive and able to silently erase existing `top_topics` data. This risk is directly introduced by the change shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] A shipped migration file was edited (whitespace/no-trailing-newline changes), altering its checksum. Environments that fingerprint migration contents (or schema dump tools comparing migration file hashes) flag the migration as tampered; more importantly it establishes the pattern of editing shipped migrations in this PR, which is how the CreateTopTopics force: true data-loss hazard was introduced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows edits to already-existing migration files: `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` has whitespace/no-newline-at-EOF changes, and `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` changes `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. Editing shipped migrations is a risky practice (can trip systems/tools that detect migration-file tampering, and `force: true` would drop/recreate the table if the migration were ever rerun), but the diff alone doesn’t prove the repo/environment actually fingerprints migration hashes or that the migration will be rerun in a way that causes breakage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` uses force on a table creation, so a re-run of the migration drops and recreates the table rather than failing loudly. If this migration is ever re-applied on a populated database (rollback/re-migrate, restored schema_migrations), all TopicEmbed rows — the mapping between embed URLs and imported topics — are destroyed, orphaning the imported topics and making feed polling re-import duplicates.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` with `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails will drop an existing `topic_embeds` table before recreating it. While migrations normally aren’t re-applied once recorded in `schema_migrations`, using `force: true` is a real, diff-grounded operational risk (e.g., if the migration is re-run in a scenario where the table already exists), and it would erase TopicEmbed rows as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update path fetches `embed.post` with no nil check, and the create path returns `post` even when `creator.create` failed (post creation errors are swallowed because `if post.present?` guards only the TopicEmbed insert, not the return). When the referenced post was deleted (e.g. via a forum purge) while the topic_embed row remains, the next feed poll crashes PostRevisor.new(nil) with NoMethodError, so the hourly PollFeed job (retry: false) dies on that item and all subsequent feed items never import.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path assigns `post = embed.post` and then (when `content_sha1` differs) unconditionally does `PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revisor.revise!(...)` with no nil guard (new file `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, else-branch). If the `topic_embeds` row exists but the referenced `posts` row was deleted (no FK shown; only `post_id null: false` in the migration), `embed.post` can be `nil`, leading to an exception when constructing/using `PostRevisor` and aborting `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` mid-iteration. Also, on the create path, `post = creator.create` can be nil and the method returns `post` regardless, while only guarding the `TopicEmbed.create!` insert with `if post.present?`, matching the finding's observation about returning nil on failed create.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Disqus import path was rewritten to TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping the explicit `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` and the category option, so imported topics lose their original timestamps and category assignment. Anyone re-running the Disqus import after this change gets topics dated at import time and uncategorized — a field-fidelity loss relative to the previous behavior; a rollback to the old code cannot recover the original created_at values once imported.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import path changes from `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and the `:category` option handling is removed entirely. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import`, the `PostCreator` call does not pass `created_at` or `category`, so imported topics/posts will use the current time and default category behavior rather than the Disqus thread’s original timestamp/category. This is a verifiable behavior regression for the Disqus import task.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `poll_feed` calls `i.content.scrub` and `i.title` without nil guards, and passes a possibly-nil title to PostCreator. A single RSS item lacking a content or title element raises NoMethodError inside the hourly PollFeed job (retry: false), aborting the loop so all remaining items in the feed — including valid ones ordered after it — are never imported until the next hourly run hits the same item again.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` with no nil checks. If an RSS item has `content == nil`, calling `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the job mid-feed. Since `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set, the run won’t retry and later valid items in the same feed won’t be imported in that execution. The note about PostCreator is indirect but grounded: `TopicEmbed.import` constructs `PostCreator.new(..., title: title, ...)`, so a nil `i.title` would propagate there as well.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is invoked with no timeout and no size cap, so a hung or slow feed server blocks the worker indefinitely. A feed host that accepts the TCP connection but never responds hangs the PollFeed job (and any RetrieveTopic job that runs it synchronously, see topic_retriever.rb:40) for as long as the OS default socket timeout allows, stalling sidekiq workers; because `sidekiq_options retry: false` there is also no retry, so the poll silently never completes.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` performs a network fetch via `open-uri` with no explicit `read_timeout`/`open_timeout` or size limit, so the Sidekiq worker running `Jobs::PollFeed` can block indefinitely (or for a very long OS-level timeout) on a slow/hung feed server. This is amplified by `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (see `lib/topic_retriever.rb`), so a `RetrieveTopic` path can also hang while waiting for the feed poll. The diff also sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` for `PollFeed`, matching the finding that failures/hangs won’t be retried/recovered by Sidekiq.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element (Atom entries with only `<summary>`, plain RSS 2.0 items with only `<description>`), and the whole `rss.items.each` loop aborts on the first such item. One malformed/short item anywhere in the feed stops processing of every subsequent item in that poll — all later articles are silently dropped while the job 'succeeds'; with `retry: false` the work is lost until the next hour and then fails the same way, so the tail of the feed is never imported.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` inside `rss.items.each`. If a `SimpleRSS` item lacks a `content` field (e.g., Atom entries with only `<summary>` or RSS items with only `<description>`), `i.content` can be `nil`, and `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the loop/job and preventing subsequent items from being imported during that run. There is no rescue/fallback to `i.summary`/`i.description` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `TopicEmbed.import` returns nil with no log and no error result when the URL doesn't match `/^https?:///`, so callers like the disqus importer and PollFeed silently skip the item while treating the run as success. The disqus import path (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor` now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote` → `import`) silently skips any thread whose link is not http(s) — the importer prints 'Creating ...' then skips it, and PollFeed drops every non-http item with no error surfaced; operators see a completed import with missing content and nothing to debug.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the first line `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) causes a silent `nil` return for any non-http(s) URL. Callers do not surface this: `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)` and ignores the return value, so such items are dropped with no error/log; `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` and only proceeds `if post.present?`, so a `nil` result means the thread is effectively skipped after printing "Creating ..." with no further indication. This creates an operator-visible 'successful run with missing content' failure mode grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `fetch_http` crashes with NoMethodError on nil when `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is blank, because `.downcase` is called before the blank check that PollFeed's `execute` performs but this path does not. With embeddable_host set but embed_by_username blank (a configuration that the /embed/best endpoint's `ensure_embeddable` filter does not reject), the RetrieveTopic job dies with an unhandled exception; the user's browser sits on the loading page and reloads every 30s forever with no error ever surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `fetch_http` does `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` unconditionally: `user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first`. If `embed_by_username` is `nil` or blank, this raises `NoMethodError` before the subsequent `return if user.blank?`. The `/embed/best` path (`EmbedController#best`) only enforces `embeddable_host` and referer host in `ensure_embeddable` and can enqueue `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` even when `embed_by_username` is unset, so the job can die and the client will remain on `loading.html.erb` (reload loop) without surfacing an error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 60-second throttle key is committed via `setnx` before the retrieval is attempted, so a failed fetch burns the throttle and subsequent requests no-op 'successfully' for 60 seconds. When `fetch_http`/`import_remote` raises (network error, readability failure) or silently returns nil (user blank, invalid URL), the redis key is already set, so every retry from the embedding page's 30s reload hits `retrieved_recently?` true and does nothing — the user is stuck on the 'Loading Discussion' page reloading indefinitely with the failure completely invisible.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, the throttle check runs before attempting the actual work: `perform_retrieve unless (invalid_host? || retrieved_recently?)`. In `retrieved_recently?`, the Redis key `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` is created via `$redis.setnx` and `$redis.expire(..., 60)` immediately when the call is *allowed* (it returns `false` after setting the key). That means the 60s throttle is consumed even if `perform_retrieve` later does nothing (`fetch_http` returns early when `user.blank?`) or raises (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` and `Readability::Document.new(...)` with no rescue). Subsequent requests/jobs within 60s will see the key, `retrieved_recently?` returns `true`, and `perform_retrieve` is skipped, matching the reported stuck/hidden-failure behavior (especially combined with `loading.html.erb` reloading every 30s).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `perform_retrieve` runs the entire PollFeed synchronously inside the RetrieveTopic job (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`), so one embed page view triggers a full feed download and a TopicEmbed.import for every feed item. Each first-time embed view pays the cost of importing the whole RSS feed (N remote-fetched articles if the feed doesn't contain the URL and it falls through to fetch_http — a full second remote fetch per item); a site with a large feed gets a long-running job per new embed URL, multiplying outbound requests and blocking workers; if PollFeed raises, fetch_http never runs for that URL.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` running the scheduled feed poller synchronously via `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling through to `fetch_http` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` downloads/parses the entire feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) and iterates all `rss.items`, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for each item (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). This means a single embed retrieval can trigger a full feed scan/import work on the same worker, which is a concrete performance/architecture concern; also, any exception in PollFeed would prevent reaching `fetch_http` since it’s not rescued. However, the finding overstates some behavior: PollFeed does not do an extra remote fetch per feed item in this diff (it imports from `i.content`/`i.link`), so the “second remote fetch per item” part is not verifiable from the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The origin check uses substring containment (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`), and the resize handler is the only feedback channel for iframe height. Any origin that is a substring of the Discourse URL (e.g. a discourseUrl of `http://forum.evil.com` accepts messages from origin `http://evil.com`... more precisely a page hosted at an origin that appears as a substring of discourseUrl) can drive the iframe's height arbitrarily; and if the inner page's postMessage never fires (blocked, slow), the iframe stays at default height with content clipped and no error shown. The containment weakness is primarily Security's; the silent stuck-height is the runtime-reliability cost.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is a substring containment check rather than an exact origin match. This is a weaker/incorrect origin validation pattern for `postMessage` and can accept unintended origins if they appear as a substring of `discourseUrl` (security-sensitive, since the handler then trusts `e.data.height` to set `iframe.height`). Additionally, the iframe is created with `scrolling = "no"` and no explicit height until a postMessage arrives, so if the resize message never arrives the embed can remain clipped with no fallback behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading page blindly reloads every 30 seconds with no failure counter and no error state. When the RetrieveTopic job permanently fails (blank embed_by_username, unreachable article URL, non-http URL), the embedding site's visitors get an infinite reload loop of the 'Loading Discussion' page — the failure is never surfaced to the user or to the operator, since the job's exception is the only trace.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` which unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30s with no max-attempts or error UI. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it always enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `loading`. But retrieval can permanently make no progress without raising (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early if `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` lookup yields no user, which will happen when `embed_by_username` is blank), leaving `topic_id_for_embed` nil forever and causing an infinite reload loop for visitors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] On the update path, `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs after `revisor.revise!` without checking its return value, and `revise!` returns false without raising when the revision doesn't happen. If the revise fails or is skipped (e.g. post record soft-deleted, save fails), the new sha1 is committed anyway, so the changed content is permanently lost — the next poll compares against the updated sha1 and considers the stale post current, a silent dropped update reported as success.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally calls `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` when the sha differs. The diff shows `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` early (`return false if not should_revise?`) and `update_post` now uses `@post.save` (non-bang) which can fail without raising. Because `TopicEmbed.import` does not check the return value or whether the post was actually updated, it can commit the new `content_sha1` even when the post revision is skipped/failed, causing future polls to think content is current and silently dropping the update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` with no timeout and no size cap on a URL that originates from the RSS feed or the request parameter path. A large or slow article page (or a feed-entry link pointing at a huge file) is read fully into memory and read for as long as the socket stays open, blocking the RetrieveTopic/PollFeed worker — unbounded download with no timeout on the background request path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces network fetches that fully read remote content with `open(...).read` and no explicit timeout/size cap. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` it does `open(url).read` on `url` coming from `TopicRetriever` (`@embed_url` originates from the `embed_url` request param) and from feed entry links via `Jobs::PollFeed` -> `TopicEmbed.import(...)`/`TopicRetriever.fetch_http`. This can block Sidekiq workers and consume unbounded memory on large/slow responses (a practical DoS/perf/security defect) because nothing in the shown code enforces timeouts or limits.
